Currently, the iOS 27.2 beta has added a Siri AI "suggested actions" feature in the Messages app. Some people find it useful, while others find it annoying.

A developer who has previously discovered many unreleased features has found that Apple is preparing some new options to try to satisfy everyone...

Suggested actions in Messages

The suggested actions feature has been present since the first beta of iOS 27, but Apple later removed it after receiving complaints that some suggestions were rather random. It then returned in the iOS 27.2 beta. Apple's description of this is as follows:

In the first example above, someone in a group chat asked everyone to go buy something and to also bring along items that were left behind last time. The Messages app will then provide one-tap options to directly "add to Reminders" or "add to Notes". In the second example, someone asked to share specific photos, and the Messages app will provide a button that takes you directly to search for photos that match the criteria.

Two ways to hide suggestions you don't want to see

Leaker pdfu discovered some new control options in iOS 27.2 beta 3 that allow you to selectively turn off the suggestions you don't want to see.

These options let you toggle on or off by category yourself, and also let Siri AI automatically monitor which suggestions you have actually used and which you haven't, then automatically hide categories you haven't used in the past 30 days.

These options are not yet officially enabled in the beta, but are very likely to roll out soon.

9to5Mac's view

I myself definitely belong to the camp that finds these suggestions more annoying than useful most of the time, but at the same time I also know some friends who really like this feature, so this change should be able to satisfy everyone.
